bullets.title: Broad Market Selloff: S&P -2.7%, VIX +28% to 33.69; Tech/AI Stocks Lead Decline
bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 2.7% to 7,005.93 with VIX surging 27.8% to 33.69, reflecting a broad risk-off session. Semis were hit hardest — SOXX -5.4%, with MU -9%, AMD -7.3%, ARM -7%, NVDA -6.1%, TSM -5.8%. Tech leaders including AVGO, ORCL, GOOGL, and BKNG all hit 52-week lows, with IONQ -56% and CRWV -48% YTD among the worst drawdowns.

bullets.title: Growth vs. Non-Growth Rotation Accelerating: Down 18% Since Oct 7
bullets.body: The Growth/Non-Growth ratio fell another 4% today, extending a cumulative 18% decline since October 7. Basic Materials, Energy, Financials, and Industrials are outperforming Tech and Consumer Discretionary as the market rotates away from AI/growth names toward cyclical and value sectors.

bullets.title: PCE In Line, Q3 GDP Revised to 4.3% — Economy Too Hot for Fed Comfort
bullets.body: October core PCE rose 0.29% MoM (3.26% YoY, up from 3.14%), with ~50-52% of PCE categories growing above 3% and the 16% trimmed mean notably hot. Q3 GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3% from 3.4% (prior flash 3.5%), driven by consumer spending (4.2%) and capex (16.1%); nominal GDP running ~6.3% is inconsistent with returning to 2% inflation. National profit margins hit all-time highs at 17.4% in Q3, up 1.8ppt YoY.

bullets.title: Fed Likely Cuts 25bps in December But Signals Hawkish Path; Fed Put Far Out of Money
bullets.body: The in-line PCE print keeps a December 25bps cut on the table, with the Fed expected to signal continued cuts while maintaining hawkish rhetoric — which is viewed as easier to reverse than a 50bps move. However, with nominal growth near 6.3% and inflation breadth worsening, the Fed will remain restrictive until convinced disinflation resumes; a significant market decline would be welcomed by the Fed as a cooling mechanism, and the current selloff is not yet severe enough to cancel the December cut.

bullets.title: AI Capex Cycle at Inflection: $1.4T in 2027 But Growth Decelerates After; Financing Stress Emerging
bullets.body: JPM forecasts AI capex doubling to $1.4T in 2027 with 23 GW under construction and 97 GW committed, but growth rates decelerate materially in 2028+. Financing stress is real: HSBC sold $300M datacenter loans at 85 cents on the dollar, an ING $500M auction failed, and Anthropic's Nexus Hubbard bond sale was delayed and backstopped by Google. Loan-to-cost ratios are expected to decline from 70-95% to ~60%, requiring $2.9T in cumulative equity over five years.

bullets.title: AI Demand Signal Deteriorating: Token Spend Leveled Off, Pricing Collapsed Despite Massive Buildout
bullets.body: Token spend has leveled off and token pricing has collapsed even as contracted compute commitments remain enormous — suggesting Jevons Paradox is not holding for AI inference. GPU pricing on Asia data centers has fallen ~7% with NVDA B300 lead times now at 40 weeks, and SemiAnalysis argues supply (not demand) will drive further GPU price declines, marking the end of surge pricing. Frontier model revenue run-rating near $150B but not translating into faster top-line growth for the ecosystem, creating a mid-cycle perception problem.

bullets.title: DELL Blowout Quarter But Stock -7%: $132B AI Backlog, FY28 EPS 27% Above Consensus
bullets.body: Dell reported F3Q revenue of $54.9B (vs $49.3B est.), EPS $9.45 (vs $6.57 est.), and raised FY27 revenue guidance to $202B with AI server revenue at $78B. The AI server backlog stands at $132B with ~7,500+ customers (up ~15% QoQ). FY28 EPS guided at $39.68, 27% above consensus. Despite the blowout, the stock is -7% premarket as the market debates CY28 DRAM pricing risk and sustainability of AI server demand.

bullets.title: NVDA: Government Equity Stake Speculation, California AG Investigation, CEO Pardon Discussion
bullets.body: Trump has indicated the US could pursue an equity stake in NVDA and is open to pardoning CEO Jensen Huang if necessary. California's AG is separately investigating NVDA despite Huang's recent reinstatement. Congressional pressure on Nvidia over export curbs and open-weight AI policy debate adds to regulatory overhang.

bullets.title: AI Capex Now ~1/3 of Aggregate GDP Growth; Core Demand ex-AI Solid at ~2.9%
bullets.body: Approximately one-third of Q3 aggregate demand growth is attributable to AI (IP development and data center capex), accounting for just over half of the 20bps upward revision to 4-quarter GDP growth (now 2.3%). Final sales to private domestic purchasers less computers/peripherals growing at a 2.9% four-quarter rate, suggesting core non-AI demand remains stable.

bullets.title: META/AMZN Muse Integration Talks Resume; Google Surpasses OpenAI in Model Spend
bullets.body: Meta and Amazon are in active discussions to restore Muse to Amazon's platform (blocked two months ago), with launch expected in 2027. Muse has expanded to UK, Japan, Singapore, Canada, Australia, Mexico and is now live on Instagram. Separately, Google models commanded >50% of OpenRouter spend for the first time since June, driven by Gemini 4 Neon and Carbon releases; Google Neon set a Day-1 usage record on paid APIs.

bullets.title: Holiday Spending Tracking +12% YoY; K-Shaped Consumer with AI Shopping Surging
bullets.body: Citi's holiday survey shows 2026 spending +12% vs 2025, with higher-income households spending more and lower-income households less (K-shape). AI-driven retail traffic generates 83% higher revenue per visit vs non-AI per Adobe data, and 33% of US consumers now use AI for shopping vs 19% one year ago. BFCM 2025 showed 27% GMV growth on Shopify; market expects >30% in 2026 as a key signal.

bullets.title: US Hotel RevPAR +13.4% YoY; Vegas Strip Surges +36.5% — Experiences Demand Intact
bullets.body: US weekly RevPAR rose 13.4% YoY for the week ended 11/21 (vs 12.9% prior week) on 450bps harder comps; two-year stack improved to +13.4% from +8.4%. Vegas Strip RevPAR surged 36.5% YoY with Mon-Wed strength exceeding +100%. Goldman's Consumer Experiences basket is outperforming the S&P 500 and positioning remains light, suggesting room for further upside despite higher 2027 input cost risks.

bullets.title: New Home Sales Beat at 701k (+14.2% MoM) But September Revised Down Sharply; Q4 Residential Investment -5.7%
bullets.body: October new home sales jumped 14.2% MoM to 701k, beating consensus of 650k, with the South driving the entire national gain and prices falling 0.3% MoM to $391k. However, September was revised down sharply from 676k to 614k, leaving YTD sales -3% vs 2025. Q4 real residential investment now tracks -5.7% QoQ SAAR, with Morgan Stanley expecting new home sales down 4% YoY in 2026 before rebounding to +2% in 2027.

bullets.title: IT Budget Rotation: Security and AI-Native Solutions Win; Incumbent App Software Loses
bullets.body: CIO surveys show IT budgets are prioritizing hardware, cybersecurity, and AI-native solutions over incumbent application software. This dynamic is weighing on names like CRM (Agentforce adoption improving but ROI/pricing uncertainty limiting broad adoption), WDAY (F4Q subscription guide of +10% vs F3Q +13% signals deceleration, shorter contract commitments), and ADSK (Q4 organic growth slowing). KeyBanc's software preview notes AI free-tier friction slowing customer spending and SEO challenges.

bullets.title: WDAY Softer Exit Rate: F4Q Subscription Guide Misses, Shorter Commitments Signal Structural Deceleration
bullets.body: Workday guided F4Q subscription revenue at $2.600B, missing consensus, with growth decelerating from F3Q's 13% to ~10%. Five-year cohorts are renewing at approximately three years (shorter), and deferred revenue growth slowed to ~10%. AI ARR is $750M+ at 130% YoY but appears to be cannibalizing non-AI spending. FY28 guidance reiterates ~11% growth, though the softer exit rate is a concern; multiple analysts cut PTs to ~$175-200.

bullets.title: Tariffs Broadening: China, EU Manufactured Goods in Scope; E-Commerce Margins at Risk
bullets.body: The US is preparing to raise tariffs on China, EU, and other economies with broader scope for Chinese products, pressuring e-commerce sourcing costs and margins. This creates headwinds for AMZN, ETSY, and other marketplace platforms reliant on manufactured goods imports, while also creating near-term risk for apparel retailers heading into 2027 (flagged across ANF, DKS commentary).

bullets.title: Data Center Sector Faces Multiple Headwinds: Zoning Bans, Export Compliance Reviews, Pricing Pressure
bullets.body: San Francisco extended a data center zoning moratorium; Prologis' Georgia Project Sail faces a January special election referendum to ban data centers; major banks are reviewing data center clients for US chip export compliance. Asia GPU pricing has fallen ~7% as operators offload excess capacity, CoreWeave bonds hit record lows, and Anthropic's IPO rally is unraveling amid rising infrastructure cost concerns.

bullets.title: Technical Analyst: Durable Bottom Not Yet in Place; Banks (KBW) Key to Market Direction
bullets.body: Technical analysis indicates durable bottom set-ups are not quite in place based on current metrics. The KBW bank index is viewed as critical to whether a broader market rally is possible — the market is unlikely to sustainably rebound if banks continue declining. Multiple indicator readings are not yet at extreme levels despite significant price action declines.

bullets.title: Q4 Real PCE Tracking 1.7% Annualized, Down from 2.5% Prior; Real Spending Flat in October
bullets.body: October real PCE came in marginally negative, missing expectations by 10-20bps, with motor vehicles down 1.48%. Q4 real PCE is now tracking 1.7% annualized (assuming 2% sequential in November/December) versus a prior estimate of just under 2.5%. Real PCE ex-autos remains at 2.5% annualized, suggesting autos drove most of the miss. The saving rate edged up to 4.1% from 3.6%, while personal income beat at +0.73% MoM.

bullets.title: BofA LatAm 2027 Outlook: Brazil Near-Stagnation, Mexico AI Export Growth, Region Broadly Downgraded
bullets.body: BofA forecasts Brazil GDP slowing to 0.3% in 2027 (from 1.6% in 2026) with Selic remaining at 13.75% through 3Q27 before easing to 13.25% YE. Mexico outperforms at 2.2% GDP growth driven by AI-related exports. Brazil, Peru, and Colombia were downgraded to marketweight from overweight; Mexico was upgraded to marketweight from underweight. Ibovespa target set at 190k and Mexbol at 80k for YE2027.
